material_claims.proposition: A person must be assumed to have capacity unless lack of capacity is established.
material_claims.exact_normalized_span_text: a person must be assumed to have capacity unless it is established that he lacks capacity.

material_claims.proposition: A person is not unable to decide unless all practicable decision-support steps have been taken without success.
material_claims.exact_normalized_span_text: a person is not to be treated as unable to make a decision unless all practicable steps to help him to do so have been taken without success.

material_claims.proposition: Capacity is matter- and time-specific and turns on inability caused by impairment or disturbance of mind or brain.
material_claims.exact_normalized_span_text: for the purposes of this act, a person lacks capacity in relation to a matter if at the material time he is unable to make a decision for himself in relation to the matter because of an impairment of, or a disturbance in the functioning of, the mind or brain.

material_claims.proposition: The impairment or disturbance may be permanent or temporary.
material_claims.exact_normalized_span_text: it does not matter whether the impairment or disturbance is permanent or temporary.

material_claims.proposition: Lack of capacity is decided on the balance of probabilities.
material_claims.exact_normalized_span_text: in proceedings under this act or any other enactment, any question whether a person lacks capacity within the meaning of this act must be decided on the balance of probabilities.

material_claims.proposition: A person is unable to decide if unable to understand, retain, use or weigh relevant information, or communicate the decision.
material_claims.exact_normalized_span_text: for the purposes of section 2, a person is unable to make a decision for himself if he is unable- a to understand the information relevant to the decision, b to retain that information, c to use or weigh that information as part of the process of making the decision, or d to communicate his decision (whether by talking, using sign language or any other means).

material_claims.proposition: Understanding must be assessed after an explanation appropriate to the person's circumstances.
material_claims.exact_normalized_span_text: a person is not to be regarded as unable to understand the information relevant to a decision if he is able to understand an explanation of it given to him in a way that is appropriate to his circumstances (using simple language, visual aids or any other means).

material_claims.proposition: Relevant information includes reasonably foreseeable consequences of deciding either way or failing to decide.
material_claims.exact_normalized_span_text: the information relevant to a decision includes information about the reasonably foreseeable consequences of- a deciding one way or another, or b failing to make the decision.

bindings.unresolved_scope_note: These provisions govern best interests and protection for care or treatment acts, but do not by themselves resolve every emergency-treatment, necessity or clinical-negligence question.

material_claims.proposition: The decision-maker must consider all relevant circumstances when determining best interests.
material_claims.exact_normalized_span_text: the person making the determination must consider all the relevant circumstances and, in particular, take the following steps.

material_claims.proposition: Best-interests analysis must consider reasonably ascertainable past and present wishes, beliefs, values and other likely decision factors.
material_claims.exact_normalized_span_text: he must consider, so far as is reasonably ascertainable- a the person's past and present wishes and feelings (and, in particular, any relevant written statement made by him when he had capacity), b the beliefs and values that would be likely to influence his decision if he had capacity, and c the other factors that he would be likely to consider if he were able to do so.

material_claims.proposition: Where practicable and appropriate, specified carers, interested persons, attorneys and deputies must be consulted about best interests.
material_claims.exact_normalized_span_text: he must take into account, if it is practicable and appropriate to consult them, the views of- a anyone named by the person as someone to be consulted on the matter in question or on matters of that kind, b anyone engaged in caring for the person or interested in his welfare, c any donee of a lasting power of attorney granted by the person, and d any deputy appointed for the person by the court, as to what would be in the person's best interests and, in particular, as to the matters mentioned in subsection (6).

material_claims.proposition: Section 5 applies to an act connected with care or treatment only where reasonable capacity-assessment steps are taken and the actor reasonably believes that capacity is lacking and the act is in the person's best interests.
material_claims.exact_normalized_span_text: if a person ("d") does an act in connection with the care or treatment of another person ("p"), the act is one to which this section applies if- a before doing the act, d takes reasonable steps to establish whether p lacks capacity in relation to the matter in question, and b when doing the act, d reasonably believes- i that p lacks capacity in relation to the matter, and ii that it will be in p's best interests for the act to be done.

material_claims.proposition: If section 5 applies, the actor does not incur liability that would not have arisen had the person possessed capacity and consented.
material_claims.exact_normalized_span_text: d does not incur any liability in relation to the act that he would not have incurred if p- a had had capacity to consent in relation to the matter, and b had consented to d's doing the act.

material_claims.proposition: Section 5 does not exclude civil or criminal liability resulting from negligence in doing the act.
material_claims.exact_normalized_span_text: nothing in this section excludes a person's civil liability for loss or damage, or his criminal liability, resulting from his negligence in doing the act.

material_claims.proposition: Section 5 does not affect the operation of advance decisions to refuse treatment.
material_claims.exact_normalized_span_text: nothing in this section affects the operation of sections 24 to 26 (advance decisions to refuse treatment).
